title: LAMMPS fix nvt
content: fix nvt is used for Nose-Hoover style NVT time integration. It controls temperature and is commonly used for constant-volume molecular dynamics after initialization or equilibration.

title: LAMMPS fix npt
content: fix npt performs Nose-Hoover style NPT integration and controls both temperature and pressure. It is commonly used when density or cell volume should relax during equilibration.

title: LAMMPS fix nph
content: fix nph controls pressure without thermostatting temperature. It can be used when enthalpy-like pressure evolution is needed and temperature control is handled elsewhere.

title: LAMMPS compute msd
content: compute msd calculates the mean-squared displacement of atoms and is widely used to analyze diffusion behavior from molecular dynamics trajectories.

title: LAMMPS compute rdf
content: compute rdf evaluates the radial distribution function. It is commonly used to characterize short-range order and local structure in liquids, amorphous phases, or crystals.

title: LAMMPS pair_style overview
content: pair_style selects the form of interatomic interactions in LAMMPS. The correct pair style must be compatible with the chosen potential file and target material class.

title: LAMMPS pair_coeff
content: pair_coeff assigns the actual parameters or files used by the active pair_style. A common source of runtime errors is mismatch between pair_style, pair_coeff, atom types, and potential files.

title: LAMMPS pair_style eam and eam/alloy
content: EAM-style pair styles are widely used for metallic systems and alloys. In LAMMPS they are configured with pair_style eam, eam/alloy, or related variants depending on the parameterization.

title: LAMMPS thermo_style
content: thermo_style configures which thermodynamic quantities are printed during a run, such as temperature, potential energy, total energy, and pressure. It is essential for monitoring stability and convergence.

title: LAMMPS dump custom
content: dump custom writes trajectory information such as atom id, type, and coordinates. It is commonly used when downstream visualization or analysis in OVITO is required.

title: LAMMPS timestep
content: The timestep command sets the MD integration step. Too large a timestep is a common reason for unstable dynamics, lost atoms, or non-physical pressure and temperature spikes.

title: LAMMPS velocity create
content: velocity create initializes atomic velocities according to a target temperature and random seed. It is usually applied before equilibration for a fresh MD run.

title: LAMMPS units metal
content: units metal is a common choice for metallic systems. In this unit style, temperature is in Kelvin, distance in Angstrom, time in picoseconds, and energy in eV.

title: LAMMPS lost atoms error
content: Lost atoms usually indicate unstable dynamics or atoms leaving the simulation domain. Common causes include too large timestep, poor initial structure, excessive temperature, bad boundary choices, unsuitable potential settings, or insufficient equilibration.

title: LAMMPS non-numeric pressure error
content: Non-numeric pressure often means the simulation has become numerically unstable. Typical causes include overlapping atoms, too aggressive timestep, wrong units, invalid pair parameters, or an unrealistic starting configuration.

title: LAMMPS pair coeff missing
content: Pair coeff missing or not set errors usually mean that pair_coeff lines do not cover all atom types required by the active pair_style. Check atom type count, element mapping order, and potential file compatibility.

title: LAMMPS incorrect args for pair coefficients
content: Incorrect args for pair coefficients usually means the number or order of pair_coeff arguments does not match the active pair_style. It can also happen when an EAM file is used with the wrong substyle.

title: LAMMPS cannot open potential file
content: Cannot open potential file usually means the file path is wrong, the file is missing, or the working directory does not match the expected potentials directory. Verify POTENTIALS_DIR, file permissions, and exact file name.

title: LAMMPS neighbor list overflow
content: Neighbor list overflow is often a sign of severe structural overlap or exploding dynamics. Before increasing neighbor settings, first check the initial structure, timestep, temperature ramp, and potential quality.

title: EAM potential for metallic systems
content: The embedded-atom method is widely used for metallic systems such as Al, Cu, Ni, Fe and many alloys. It is a natural first choice for simple elemental-metal diffusion, heating, and equilibration demonstrations in LAMMPS.

title: Lennard-Jones potential as a simple demonstration model
content: Lennard-Jones is a simple pair potential often used for generic demonstrations, noble-gas-like systems, or algorithm validation. It is usually not the first realistic choice for elemental metals such as Cu or Al.

title: OpenKIM potentials in LAMMPS
content: OpenKIM provides a wider ecosystem of tested interatomic models. It is useful when standard bundled EAM files are insufficient, but model provenance, supported species, and property targets should be checked carefully.

title: Copper is an FCC metal often modeled with EAM
content: Copper is a face-centered cubic metal. In classical MD, EAM-style potentials are a common practical choice for Cu heating, equilibration, and diffusion studies.

title: Aluminum is an FCC metal often modeled with EAM
content: Aluminum is also an FCC metal and is commonly simulated with EAM-like potentials in LAMMPS. For thermal treatment or diffusion-like demonstrations, units metal plus EAM is a conventional pairing.

title: Nickel is an FCC metal often modeled with EAM
content: Nickel is an FCC transition metal and many classical LAMMPS examples model it with EAM-style potentials. It is often used in heating, equilibration, and alloy demonstrations.

title: NVT versus NPT in molecular dynamics
content: NVT keeps the number of particles, volume, and temperature fixed, while NPT keeps number of particles, pressure, and temperature fixed. NVT is often used after the cell is already reasonable, while NPT is often used when density or box relaxation matters.

title: Typical diffusion workflow in LAMMPS
content: A typical diffusion workflow is: choose a suitable potential, build or relax a reasonable structure, equilibrate under NVT or NPT, then collect a production trajectory and compute MSD for diffusion analysis. The trajectory should also be dumped for inspection in OVITO.

title: Eutectic reaction in phase diagrams
content: A eutectic reaction occurs when a liquid transforms into two solid phases at a fixed temperature and composition. The eutectic point is a key invariant point in many binary phase diagrams.

title: Eutectoid reaction in phase diagrams
content: A eutectoid reaction occurs entirely in the solid state, where one solid phase transforms into two different solid phases at a fixed temperature and composition.

title: Peritectic reaction in phase diagrams
content: A peritectic reaction occurs when a liquid and one solid phase react to form another solid phase at a fixed temperature and composition. It is distinct from eutectoid because liquid is involved.

title: Liquidus and solidus lines
content: The liquidus line marks the boundary above which the alloy is fully liquid, while the solidus line marks the boundary below which the alloy is fully solid. Between them, mixed solid-liquid regions may appear.

title: LAMMPS minimize
content: The minimize command performs energy minimization before dynamics. For user-built crystals, alloys, surfaces, or defect structures, minimization is often a safer preflight step before velocity initialization and NVT/NPT runs.

title: LAMMPS neighbor
content: The neighbor command controls neighbor-list skin distance and binning style. Neighbor settings affect performance and can expose unstable dynamics when atoms move too far between rebuilds.

title: LAMMPS neigh_modify
content: neigh_modify controls how often neighbor lists are rebuilt and checked. When heating or deforming aggressively, more frequent checks can improve robustness, though they cannot fix a bad potential or unstable timestep.

title: LAMMPS fix langevin
content: fix langevin applies stochastic thermostatting by adding damping and random forces. It is useful for temperature control but is not a time integrator by itself, so it is commonly paired with fix nve.

title: LAMMPS fix deform
content: fix deform changes the simulation box during a run and is commonly used for strain, shear, and deformation simulations. It should be combined with compatible boundary conditions and careful timestep choices.

title: LAMMPS compute stress/atom
content: compute stress/atom estimates per-atom stress contributions. It is useful for local stress analysis, but interpretation requires attention to volume normalization and the virial definition.

title: LAMMPS compute centro/atom
content: compute centro/atom calculates the centrosymmetry parameter. It is often used to identify defects, dislocations, stacking faults, and surface atoms in crystalline metals.

title: LAMMPS compute cna/atom
content: compute cna/atom performs common-neighbor analysis to classify local crystal environments such as FCC, HCP, BCC, and disordered regions. It is sensitive to cutoff choice and thermal noise.

title: LAMMPS compute voronoi/atom
content: compute voronoi/atom computes per-atom Voronoi volumes and neighbor information. It is useful for local volume, free volume, and structural disorder analysis when the VORONOI package is available.

title: LAMMPS lattice and create_atoms
content: lattice defines a crystalline lattice and create_atoms populates atoms in a region or box. For elemental demonstration systems, using an appropriate lattice constant and structure is important before MD starts.

title: LAMMPS region and boundary
content: region defines geometric domains and boundary controls box periodicity. Many lost-atoms or vaporization-like failures are made worse by incompatible nonperiodic boundaries during high-temperature runs.

title: LAMMPS read_data and write_data
content: read_data imports a LAMMPS data file and write_data exports the current system. They are useful for reproducible workflows, handoff between tools, and preserving equilibrated structures.

title: LAMMPS replicate
content: replicate duplicates the simulation cell in x, y, and z directions. It is often used to build larger crystals from a small unit cell before equilibration or defect insertion.

title: LAMMPS out of range atoms error
content: Out of range atoms errors often appear when atoms move too far between neighbor-list rebuilds or bonded interactions stretch beyond communication cutoffs. It can indicate unstable dynamics, bad timestep, high temperature, or an unsuitable initial structure.

title: LAMMPS bond atoms missing error
content: Bond atoms missing means atoms connected by a bond could not be found on the required processors. It usually indicates an unstable bonded simulation, too large timestep, bad topology, or atoms flying apart.

title: LAMMPS illegal command or unknown command
content: Illegal command or unknown command usually means a syntax error, a command not available in the installed package set, or a mismatch between LAMMPS version and input script. Check the exact command style and installed packages.

title: LAMMPS shake atoms missing error
content: Shake atoms missing indicates constraints cannot find required atoms, often because the molecular system is unstable, timestep is too large, bonds are broken, or communication settings are insufficient.

title: MEAM potential for metals and alloys
content: MEAM extends EAM with angular contributions and can better describe some metals, alloys, and structures where simple EAM is insufficient. It requires a compatible library file and parameter file mapping.

title: Tersoff potential for covalent materials
content: Tersoff-style potentials are commonly used for covalent materials such as Si, C, and related compounds. They are not a default choice for simple metallic Cu or Al heating examples.

title: ReaxFF reactive force fields
content: ReaxFF models reactive chemistry with dynamic bond orders. It is powerful but more expensive and parameter-sensitive than simple EAM or Lennard-Jones models, so charge equilibration and validated parameter sets matter.

title: Buckingham potentials for ionic materials
content: Buckingham-style pair potentials are often used with Coulomb interactions for ionic ceramics and oxides. They require careful charge assignment and long-range electrostatics settings.

title: Machine-learning interatomic potentials in LAMMPS
content: LAMMPS supports multiple machine-learning potential interfaces. ML potentials can be accurate inside their training domain but should be treated carefully when extrapolating to high temperature, defects, or unseen compositions.

title: Iron has BCC and FCC temperature-dependent phases
content: At room temperature, alpha iron is BCC, while gamma iron is FCC at elevated temperature. Classical MD setup for Fe should match the intended phase and potential parameterization.

title: Magnesium is an HCP metal
content: Magnesium is an HCP metal at ambient conditions. In LAMMPS demonstrations, Mg generally needs a compatible EAM/MEAM-style potential rather than a generic LJ model if realistic metallic behavior is desired.

title: Zinc is an HCP metal
content: Zinc is HCP at ambient conditions and appears in many binary phase-diagram demonstrations. MD simulations should use a potential validated for Zn or Zn alloys when quantitative behavior matters.

title: Silicon is a covalent semiconductor commonly modeled with Tersoff-like potentials
content: Silicon has directional covalent bonding, so EAM is not the normal first choice. Tersoff, Stillinger-Weber, or validated machine-learning potentials are more common classical models.

title: Typical heating workflow in LAMMPS
content: A robust heating workflow usually minimizes the initial structure, assigns velocities at the starting temperature, equilibrates, ramps temperature with NVT or Langevin+NVE, dumps trajectory frames, and monitors temperature, energy, and pressure.

title: Melting simulation workflow and caveats
content: Melting simulations need careful equilibration, finite-size awareness, and a clear distinction between observed structural disorder and a thermodynamic melting point. Heating rate and boundary conditions strongly affect the apparent transition.

title: Defect or vacancy diffusion workflow
content: Vacancy diffusion studies normally require a sufficiently large relaxed supercell, one or more defects, equilibration, long production trajectories, and MSD or jump analysis. Short toy runs can demonstrate output plumbing but not quantitative diffusion.

title: Surface or slab MD setup caveats
content: Surface slab simulations use nonperiodic or shrink-wrapped boundaries in at least one direction. They require enough vacuum or boundary space and careful thermostatting to avoid atoms leaving the box during heating.

title: OVITO inspection for trajectories
content: OVITO is useful for checking whether a trajectory is physically plausible: atoms should not explode, box boundaries should look sensible, and structural coloring can reveal defects, melting, or bad initial geometry.

title: Lever rule in binary phase diagrams
content: The lever rule estimates the relative amounts of two equilibrium phases in a two-phase region from the overall composition and the tie-line end compositions.

title: Tie lines and phase equilibrium
content: A tie line connects the compositions of coexisting phases at a fixed temperature in a two-phase region. It is central to interpreting equilibrium phase fractions and compositions.

title: CALPHAD and thermodynamic databases
content: CALPHAD models phase equilibria using assessed Gibbs-energy functions stored in thermodynamic databases such as TDB files. A calculated diagram is only as reliable as the database coverage and model assumptions.

title: Gibbs energy minimization in phase equilibrium
content: Equilibrium phase calculations minimize the total Gibbs energy subject to composition, temperature, and pressure constraints. Phase boundaries appear where the stable phase assemblage changes.

title: Metastable phases versus equilibrium phase diagrams
content: Equilibrium phase diagrams show globally stable states for a chosen model and database. Metastable phases may appear in experiments or kinetic simulations but can be absent from an equilibrium calculation unless modeled explicitly.

title: Materials Project database
content: Materials Project is a computed materials database built around first-principles data. It is useful for querying structures, formation energies, phase stability, band gaps, elastic data, and related properties when a DFT-level screening perspective is needed.

title: Materials Project API querying
content: The Materials Project API supports programmatic materials queries through mp-api. Typical searches filter by chemical system, formula, material ids, energy above hull, band gap, and other computed properties.

title: NIST JARVIS-DFT database
content: JARVIS-DFT is a NIST materials database containing DFT-computed properties for many materials, including structural, energetic, electronic, elastic, dielectric, and related descriptors useful for screening and model building.

title: AFLOW materials database and API
content: AFLOW provides high-throughput computational materials data and an API ecosystem for querying calculated structures and properties. It is useful when cross-checking database-derived materials trends and descriptors.

title: matminer datasets for materials machine learning
content: matminer provides curated datasets and featurization tools for materials informatics. Its dataset summary is useful for identifying benchmark datasets for formation energy, band gap, elastic properties, and other ML tasks.

title: Formation energy in materials screening
content: Formation energy measures the energy of a compound relative to reference elemental phases. It is a key descriptor for thermodynamic stability screening, but it should be interpreted together with phase competition and energy above hull.

title: Energy above hull and phase stability
content: Energy above hull measures how far a material is above the convex hull of competing phases at the same composition space. Zero or near-zero values often indicate thermodynamic stability or plausible synthesizability, while larger values imply metastability.

title: Band gap as an electronic-structure descriptor
content: Band gap is the energy difference between occupied and unoccupied electronic states at the band edges. It is useful for classifying metals, semiconductors, and insulators, but DFT functional choice can strongly affect quantitative values.

title: Density and crystal structure descriptors
content: Density combines composition and volume information and is often used as a simple descriptor in materials screening. It should be interpreted with structure source, temperature, pressure, and possible porosity or disorder in mind.

title: Elastic tensor and elastic constants
content: The elastic tensor describes the linear relationship between stress and strain in a crystal. It can be reduced to moduli such as bulk modulus and shear modulus, but symmetry, units, and mechanical stability criteria must be handled carefully.

title: Bulk modulus and shear modulus
content: Bulk modulus measures resistance to uniform compression, while shear modulus measures resistance to shape change. They are often derived from an elastic tensor using Voigt-Reuss-Hill style averaging for polycrystalline estimates.

title: Phonons and dynamical stability
content: Phonon calculations probe lattice vibrations. Imaginary phonon modes can indicate dynamical instability of the assumed structure, while stable phonon spectra support—but do not alone prove—finite-temperature stability.

title: Vacancy defects in crystals
content: A vacancy is a missing atom on a lattice site. Vacancy concentration and migration barriers strongly affect diffusion, creep, ionic transport, and radiation damage behavior in crystalline materials.

title: Interstitial and substitutional defects
content: Interstitial defects place atoms in normally unoccupied sites, while substitutional defects replace host atoms with different species. Both can change diffusion, electronic structure, mechanical response, and phase stability.

title: Dislocations and plastic deformation
content: Dislocations are line defects that mediate plastic deformation in crystals. Their motion, interactions, and pinning by solutes or precipitates strongly influence strength and ductility.

title: Grain boundaries in polycrystalline materials
content: Grain boundaries are interfaces between crystals with different orientations. They can influence diffusion, corrosion, strength, fracture, segregation, and phase transformation behavior.

title: Stacking faults in close-packed crystals
content: A stacking fault is a planar defect where the normal stacking sequence is interrupted. In FCC and HCP metals, stacking-fault energy influences partial dislocations, twinning, and deformation mechanisms.

title: Arrhenius behavior in diffusion
content: Diffusion coefficients often follow an Arrhenius form with temperature, where the slope of ln(D) versus inverse temperature estimates an activation energy. Short MD runs may show qualitative trends but are often insufficient for accurate activation energies.

title: DFT versus classical molecular dynamics
content: DFT directly models electronic structure and is usually used for small cells and accurate energetics, while classical MD uses interatomic potentials to reach larger sizes and longer times. They answer different questions and should not be treated as interchangeable.

title: Validating interatomic potentials
content: An interatomic potential should be checked against the target chemistry, phase, temperature range, defect types, and properties of interest. A potential fitted for one phase or composition may fail badly outside its training domain.

title: High-entropy alloys
content: High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal elements and can form simple solid solutions, intermetallic phases, or complex mixtures. Phase stability depends on chemistry, temperature, entropy, enthalpy, and processing history.

title: Perovskite structure family
content: Perovskites are commonly represented by an ABX3 formula and can show diverse electronic, ionic, ferroelectric, and photovoltaic behavior. Structure tolerance and chemistry strongly affect stability and properties.

title: Two-dimensional materials
content: Two-dimensional materials are layered or atomically thin systems whose properties may differ strongly from bulk forms. Screening often uses exfoliation energy, band structure, stability, and dimensionality descriptors.

title: Battery materials screening concepts
content: Battery material screening often considers voltage, capacity, stability, ion mobility, phase changes, and compatibility with electrolytes. Database hits should be treated as candidates requiring electrochemical and synthesis validation.

title: Titanium has HCP alpha and BCC beta phases
content: Titanium is HCP in its alpha phase at lower temperatures and BCC in its beta phase at high temperature. MD and phase modeling should distinguish alpha-Ti, beta-Ti, and alloy stabilization effects.

title: Chromium is a BCC transition metal
content: Chromium is commonly treated as a BCC transition metal in classical MD demonstrations. For Cr alloys, potential choice and magnetic effects can be important limitations.

title: Cobalt can appear in HCP and FCC structures
content: Cobalt has close-packed HCP and FCC structural variants depending on temperature and conditions. MD setup should match the intended phase and potential parameterization.

title: Niobium is a BCC refractory metal
content: Niobium is a BCC refractory metal. For high-temperature MD or alloy modeling, the potential should be validated for thermal expansion, defects, and phase stability across the target range.

title: Lithium in battery and diffusion contexts
content: Lithium is central to battery materials and ion transport studies. Classical MD can model Li diffusion only when the interatomic model is validated for the host chemistry and relevant charge/interaction physics.

title: Carbon allotropes require bonding-aware potentials
content: Carbon can appear as diamond, graphite, graphene, amorphous carbon, and other allotropes. Potential choice is critical because bonding topology and hybridization control structure and properties.

title: Alumina and oxide force-field caveats
content: Alumina and related oxides often require ionic or partially charged force fields, Buckingham/Coulomb-style models, ReaxFF, or ML potentials depending on the target chemistry and property. Metallic EAM is not appropriate for oxides.

title: Ionic crystals require charge-aware interactions
content: Ionic crystals such as alkali halides are often modeled with Coulombic and short-range repulsive interactions. Charge assignment, long-range electrostatics, and compatible pair styles are central to stable simulations.

title: Stillinger-Weber potentials for covalent materials
content: Stillinger-Weber potentials are commonly used for tetrahedrally bonded materials such as silicon and some compounds. They encode angular terms and should be matched to the target element set and phase.

title: Database screening workflow for materials candidates
content: A practical database screening workflow filters by chemistry and target property, checks formation energy and energy above hull, reviews structure and calculation provenance, then validates candidates with higher-fidelity calculations or experiments.

title: Cross-checking materials properties across databases
content: When using computed materials databases, compare property definitions, calculation settings, pseudopotentials, exchange-correlation functionals, structure matching, and correction schemes before treating values as directly interchangeable.

title: Selecting an interatomic potential for MD
content: Choose an interatomic potential by matching chemistry, phase, property target, temperature range, and defect environment. Prefer documented validation data and avoid using a potential outside its fitted domain just because it runs without errors.

title: Defect calculation workflow caveats
content: Defect calculations require careful supercell size, charge state handling for electronic-structure methods, relaxation criteria, chemical potential references, and finite-size corrections. Classical MD defect studies need validated potentials and long-enough sampling.

title: MD heating curves versus equilibrium phase diagrams
content: A heating MD run can reveal structural disorder, diffusion, or apparent melting, but it is not the same as an equilibrium phase diagram. Heating rate, system size, potential accuracy, and nucleation barriers can shift apparent transitions.
source: Practical MD and thermodynamics workflow summary

title: Gibbs phase rule in phase diagrams
content: The Gibbs phase rule relates degrees of freedom, components, and phases at equilibrium. For condensed binary phase diagrams at fixed pressure, F = C - P + 1, so invariant reactions such as eutectic, peritectic, or eutectoid points have zero remaining degrees of freedom.
